s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

shortlist.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions and severe flaccid quadriparesis, consistent with BPDCN

shortlist.label: Lymphomatous meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

shortlist.label: Leukemic meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count and presence of atypical cells/blasts

shortlist.label: Neurolymphomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetric lower extremity weakness, urinary retention, and cranial nerve involvement, consistent with neurolymphomatosis

shortlist.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid analysis and severe flaccid quadriparesis

s4.champion: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy

raw.champion: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy
raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis) and the specific findings of nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots on MRI, along with the cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing 98% atypical cells/blasts, are highly suggestive of BPDCN with polyradiculopathy.

rejected.label: Lymphomatous meningitis
rejected.why: While lymphomatous meningitis could explain some neurological symptoms, it does not typically cause violaceous cutaneous lesions or the specific MRI findings seen in this case.

rejected.label: Leukemic meningitis
rejected.why: Leukemic meningitis might present with similar cerebrospinal fluid findings, but the presence of specific cutaneous lesions and the pattern of nerve root involvement point more towards BPDCN.

rejected.label: Neurolymphomatosis
rejected.why: Neurolymphomatosis involves the infiltration of lymphoma cells into the nervous system, which could explain some symptoms, but the combination of cutaneous lesions, specific MRI findings, and cerebrospinal fluid results better supports BPDCN.

rejected.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
rejected.why: While acute lymphoblastic leukemia could lead to neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement, the specific constellation of symptoms and findings, particularly the cutaneous lesions and pattern of nerve root enhancement, is more characteristic of BPDCN with polyradiculopathy.
